runs.name: Texas Instruments Incorporated
runs.entry: Price **$283.74** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **913,247,686 shares** (10-Q cover as of 2026-07-15, 0000097476-26-000152; one class; issued 1,741M less treasury 828M = 913M at 2026-06-30; the 8-K of 2026-09-17, a dividend increase, changes no count) = cap **$259,125M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y par, 2026-10-09). Pending: the all-cash Silicon Labs purchase at $231.00 a share, about $7.5B enterprise value (8-K 0001193125-26-036727, 2026-02-04; close expected first half 2027; $5B delayed-draw term loan undrawn), valued beside and not in the central figure. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. Q1 IN (more than 80,000 products to more than 100,000 customers; revenue 3.1% a year 2015-2025 with downturns in 2019, 2023 and 2024). Q2 IN (Analog decides, 83% of five-year operating profit; after-tax returns on tangible capital 60% to 105% 2014-2022, 30% in 2025; Embedded Processing margin 38.5% to 11.3%, does not decide, carried at no growth; China carried as the strongest threat: about 50% of 2025 revenue shipped into China, about 20% from customers headquartered there). Q3 against (tangible capital up about $12B since 2018 while after-tax operating profit did not grow; PP&E $2.5B to $12.3B 2016-2025 after $4.51B of CHIPS incentives netted). Q4 IN and weighs for (ten balance sheets 2016-2025: debt $3.6B to $14.1B while treasury stock rose $16.6B; inventory $1.8B to $4.8B under a stated build-ahead strategy, now falling; no adjusted earnings; quarterly guidance carried to Q5). Q5 integrity IN, ability weighs for (the capital programme the open test). Q6 against on both parts (dividends above free cash flow 2023-2025 under a policy of returning 100% of free cash flow; buybacks at no stated price, every year's average since 2021, $163 to $206, above the Q7 bottom; Silicon Labs bought for cash with negative owner cash, justified by $450M of synergies); narrower STOP does not arise (all-cash deal). **Q7 OUT on the floor:** no case earns about ten percent at $283.74 (expected return 2.4% to 4.3% by case, the most generous included). Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay, software amortization, depreciation gross of the CHIPS reduction as the maintenance guess, and the CHIPS tax credit; interest added back at 21%, a CONVENTION of the run) 2014-2025; the literal window 2021-2025 falls 13.7% a year from an upturn year the filer names, so the base is the last full cycle 2020-2023, **$6,242M** all-equity; shown growth between cycles 7.15% cut by (f) to sales growth 4.53%. Net debt $4,888M at 2026-06-30 after $2,163M of CHIPS receivables. Range **$116.70-$163.88** all-equity (equity-only $122.51-$169.87; literal window $32.71-$103.48 beside; all-spending cycle case $80.79 beside), width 1.40 to 1; fair **$74.10** all-equity ($79.76 equity-only); with Silicon Labs as if closed every figure falls $8.21 (fair $65.89). Q8 to Q12 not reached. Competitors: the 10-K names none ("dozens of large and small companies"); the analyst took Analog Devices, Microchip and NXP from the proxy's peer list, described by the filer as companies offering technology that competes with its products (all SEC filers); Infineon and Renesas named as non-filers, not read. Average operating margin 2014-2025: TXN 39.5%, ADI 26.5%, NXP 20.4%, MCHP 18.9% (rivals depressed by acquisition amortization); TXN's lead is in operating cost, not gross margin (2025 GM 57.0% against ADI 61.5%). Could not get: Silicon Labs' fiscal 2021 owner cash; a primary source for the Chinese anti-dumping investigation named only in a shareholder proposal printed in the proxy (not in the 10-K or the 2026 10-Qs); any product price series. Analyst's framework gaps for the operator: (1) no rule for rivals when the 10-K names none (the proxy peer list used; a pay peer group is chosen for pay); (2) which series defines the cycle when owner cash and revenue troughs are a year apart, and whether the closing trough is in the cycle; (3) the maintenance guess when growth fabs are being depreciated and incentives cut asset cost; (4) capital-spending tax credits inside operating cash are not covered by the Whose-tax convention; (5) whether earned government receivables reduce net debt ($2.37 a share here). Contamination declared by the analyst: a directory listing of Test Runs/ showed three other run file names of 2026-10-11 (SHOP, SPGI, TECH) and the session context showed TECH commit subjects; none opened. Eight commits (614693d8 to f07f90b0), one per question. Dispatcher quote check: 81 quoted fragments beside ids, 40 matched by the script; the 41 others are filer quotes attributed to the filer, framework wording ("ordinary returns") or window artifacts where the quote sits after the id it belongs to (M2003-149 "drop out of the game" checked in its row); eight checked by hand; no slip found; recorded, not fixed. v4.1 bands retired at the fold (TXN-rerun-band and TXN-ranks-band); v5 fair-price alert armed at $74.10. Position note filled at the fold: not held. check_framework PASS.
runs.narr: Q7 OUT on the floor at $283.74: range $116.70-$163.88 all-equity on the 2020-2023 cycle base, fair $74.10; Q1 and Q2 IN on Analog (after-tax returns on tangible capital 60% to 105% through 2022, operating margin 39.5% against rivals' 19% to 27%), China carried as the threat; Q3 and Q6 against on about $12B of added capital not yet earning, dividends above free cash flow 2023-2025, buybacks above any computed value and the all-cash Silicon Labs purchase pending. Five framework gaps reported, chief among them no rival rule when the 10-K names none and which years make a cycle.
runs.fair_label: TXN at/below $74.10: the fair price on the all-equity basis of the blind v5 purchase run of 2026-10-11 (Test Runs/2026-10-11 Run - TXN Texas Instruments.md; OUT at Q7 at $283.74; $79.76 equity-only; base the 2020-2023 cycle; $65.89 with Silicon Labs as if closed). A prompt to re-run Q7, never a verdict.
